title: Guru Nanak's birthday
hookLine: Sikhs celebrate Guru Nanak Gurpurab with processions and langar; young Nanak's true bargain was a meal for the hungry
tomorrow: a prince sat under a tree and swore not to move. until what?

lines: HUNGRY HOLY MEN ON THE ROAD.
cards: Hand a teenager some cash and tell them to make a smart deal, and anything can happen. The janamsakhis, the old life stories of Guru Nanak, tell it this way.
His father, Mehta Kalu, gives young Nanak money and sends him to market to strike a good bargain, a profitable trade. On the road, Nanak meets a group of holy men who are hungry.
He spends the money on food and feeds them.

teach.b: He comes home with empty hands, and his father is furious. Nanak's answer, in the story: this was the true bargain, sacha sauda, feeding the hungry.
Some Sikhs tell it as a seed of langar, the gurdwara's free kitchen, open to anyone.

teach.h: VAND CHHAKNA: SHARE WHAT YOU HAVE.
teach.b: In Sikhi, sharing what you have, vand chhakna, is a pillar of life, alongside honest work and remembering God's name.

Gurpurab is the day Sikhs celebrate a Guru's birth or a great event, and on Guru Nanak's Gurpurab the Guru Granth Sahib is read through without a break, a procession called nagar kirtan moves through the streets with hymns, and the langar feeds whoever comes.
The week comes home here. Retreat day, held open to compassion. Four hinges, the promise turning on time.
A new day at the equinox. Colors after a fire. Eid mubarak, with food for the poor first.
A sweet year, after a heart poured out.
And gurpurab: a birthday kept by feeding everyone.

how: On Guru Nanak Gurpurab, Sikhs hold an unbroken reading of the Guru Granth Sahib (akhand path), a nagar kirtan procession with hymns, kirtan at the gurdwara, and langar open to everyone; homes and gurdwaras are lit.

Gurpurab can only mean Guru Nanak's birthday

games.q: your cousin gets birthday money and asks what a 'true bargain' would be. which fits Nanak's story?
o: spend some of it feeding someone hungry: that was Nanak's true bargain.
invest all of it: a true bargain means the best return.
give it back: money can't have anything to do with the spirit.
games.why: sent to make a profitable deal, Nanak fed hungry holy men and called that the true bargain.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who fed you this week: at a table, with a plate at the door, with a meal you didn't pay for. Thank each one quietly by name. Then choose one meal you could share freely before the week is out.

wordCard.voice: Guru Nanak's birthday: Sikhs call it Gurpurab, kept with hymns in the streets and a free meal for everyone.
